Lobsang Jampel Gyatso (Blo-bzang ‘jam-dpal rgya-mtso,), n.d. The Daymaker that Opens a Thousand Wondrous Blooms: A Catalog of the Holy Objects contained in the Inner Sanctum at the Heart of that Wish-Giving Jewel, the Precious Tomb of that High Being, the Victor Supreme, as well as the Shrine and its Objects (rGyal-ba mchog gi bdag-nyid gang de’i sku-gdung rin-po-che yid-bzhin nor-bu snying-por bzhugs-pa’i mchod-sdong chen-po rten dang brten-par bcas-pa’i dkar-chag Ngo-mtsar ‘dab-stong ‘byed-pa’i nyin-byed,), ACIP S12224, 42 ff.
Je Lobsang Tenpa (rJe Blo-bzang bstan-pa,), fl. 1750. A Biography of Lord Tsongkapa (rJe’i rnam-thar,), 47 ff. Listed by Longdol Lama (B64).

Ngari Shabdrung Lobsang Tenpay Gyeltsen (mNga’-ris zhabs-drung Blo-bzang bstan-pa’i rgyal-mtsan,), fl. 1690. Said by Longdol Lama (entry B64) to have composed a Biography of Lord Tsongkapa (rJe yi rnam-thar,), 13 ff. This would appear to be the same text listed by Gyalwang Trinley Namgyal in his Great Biography: the Thousand Rays of Sunlight that Nourish the Lotus Garden of Those with Enough Goodness within Them (sKal-ldan pad-tsal rgyas-pa’i ‘od-stong,), by the “Revered Follower of Shakyamuni from Ngari, Jamyang Nyima Tenpay Gyeltsen” (mNga’-ris sh’ak-btzun ‘Jam-dbyangs nyi-ma bstan-pa’i rgyal-mtsan,).

Ta-tsak Rinpoche Lobsang Tupten Wangchuk (rTa-tsag rin-po-che Blo-bzang thub-bstan dbang-phyug), n.d. A Hundred and Eight Amazing Tales of the Life of Je Tsongkapa (rNam-thar Ngo-mtsar-ba’i gtam brgya rtza brgyad-pa,), reported by Gyalwang Trinley Namgyal in his Great Biography.

Radreng Achitu Nomohan Lobsang Yeshe Tenpa Rabgye (Rva-sgreng Aa-chi-thu No-mo-han Blo-bzang ye-shes bstan-pa rab-rgyas,), 1759-1815. Verses for Supplication to the Lamas of the Lineage for a Variety of Subjects: The Teachings on the Steps of the Path, as found in the Great Book on the Steps of the Path to Enlightenment; The Hundred-Section Supplication to the Lamas of the Lineage of the Instruction on the Profound Path of the Practice of the Lama in the Tradition of Se, along with its Instructions; A Supplication to the Lamas of the Lineage of the Great Seal; the Quartet of Commentaries; the Total Illumination of the Hidden Meaning; the Teaching on the Stage of Creation in the System of Highest Bliss (Sanvara), according to Tang Sakpa; the Empowerment into the Practice of Victory over Every Demon; and the Thirteen Angels of the Secret Teachings of the Lord of Terror (Bhairava)—along with Verses that are to be Added at the End of a Number of Other Supplications to Lamas of Lineages (Byang-chub lam-rim chen-mo sogs lam-rim skor dang, Sras rgyud-lugs kyi zab-lam bla-ma’i rnal-’byor gyi khrid bcas kyi rgyud-’debs le-tsan brgya dang, phyag-chen gsol-’debs, ‘Grel-pa bzhi-sbrags, sBas-don kun-gsal, Thang-sag-pa’i bDe-mchog bskyed-rim, bDud las rnam-rgyal gyi dbang, ‘Jigs-byed lha bcu-gsum-ma bcas kyi brgyud-’debs, gzhan yang bla-brgyud ‘ga’-zhig gi gsham du mthud-rgyu tsigs-bcad bcas,), ACIP S06226, ff. 293a-436b.

Panchen Lodru Leksang (Pa -chen Blo-gros legs-bzang,), fl. 1420. Listed by Master Jamyang Shepa and by Gyalwang Trinley Namgyal as having written a biography of Je Tsongkapa; the latter says it was named Highly Secret Words of Wonder, for Your Entertainment (Rab-gsang rmad-byung gtam gyi dga’-ston,), 19 ff. Longdol Lama (entry B64) refers to a biography by this author without mentioning its title; he gives a very similar title to another biography, by Jedrung Ngawang Chukyi Je (entry 51).

Longdol Lama Ngawang Lobsang (Klong-rdol bla-ma Ngag-dbang blo-bzang,), 1719-1794. A List of Those High Beings who have Come Into Our World in the Lands of India and Tibet in order to Uphold the Teachings (rGya bod du byon-pa’i bstan-’dzin gyi skyes-bu dam-pa rnams kyi mtsan-tho,), ACIP S06552, ff. 353a-418b.

Longdol Lama Ngawang Lobsang (Klong-rdol bla-ma Ngag-dbang blo-bzang,), 1719-1794. A List to Describe the History of the Great Patrons of the Teachings—both Kings and their Ministers—from both India and Tibet (rGya bod du bstan-pa’i sbyin-bdag rgyal-blon ji-ltar byung-tsul gyi mtsan-tho,), ACIP S06553, ff. 419a-460a.

Longdol Lama Ngawang Lobsang (Klong-rdol bla-ma Ngag-dbang blo-bzang,), 1719-1794. A Rough Outline of the Contents of the Collected Works of Selected Lamas from the Keepers of the Word—the Kadampas; and the Virtuous Way—the Gelukpas (bKa’-gdams-pa dang dGe-lugs-pa’i bla-ma rags-rim gyi gsung-‘bum dkar-chag), ACIP S6555, ff. 495a-638b.

Kedrup Rinpoche Metrepa (mKhas-grub rin-po- che Me-tre-pa,), n.d. A Biography of Je Tsongkapa (rJe’i rnam-thar,), listed by Gyalwang Trinley Namgyal in his Great Biography. It is not clear whether this is Kedrup Je himself.

Mu-ge Samten Gyatso (dMu-dge bSam-gtan rgya-mtso,), 1914-1993. The New Sun of True Words that Open the Lotus Blooms of Faith: A Biography of the High and Holy One, Jikme Trinle Gyatso, Good and Glorious (rJe-btzun ‘Jigs-med ‘phrin-las rgya-mtso dpal bzang-po’i rnam-par thar-ba Dad-pa’i pad-mo bzhad-pa’i bden-gtam nyi-ma gzhon-nu,), ACIP S12332, 402 pp.

Mu-ge Samten Gyatso (dMu-dge bSam-gtan rgya-mtso,), 1914-1993. A Song of the Gods, Filled with Meaning: Chronicles of the Monastery of Taktsa Trashi Chusang Ling (sTag-tsa bkra-shis chos-bzang gling gi gdan-rabs Don-ldan lha’i rol-mo,), ACIP S12340, pp.464-572.
Ne-nying Chuje Kunga Delek (gNas-rnying chos-rje Kun-dga’ bde-legs,), d. 1496. Entry Point for Those of Faith (Dad-pa’i ‘jug-ngogs,), reported by Master Jamyang Shepa, and also listed in MHTL, 62 ff.

Rongpa Ngawang Chudrak Gyatso (Rong-pa Ngag-dbang chos-grags rgya-mtso,), n.d. A Bouquet of Flowers Picked on the Path of Classical Poetry (sNyan-dngags kyi lam las drangs-pa Me-tog ‘chun-po,), listed by Gyalwang Trinley Namgyal as a source in the Great Biography.

Jedrung Ngawang Chukyi Wangchuk (rJe drung Ngag-dbang chos-kyi dbang-phyug), n.d. Said by Longdol Lama (B64) to have written a biography called A Hundred Amazing Tales of Wonder (Ngo-tsar rmad-du byung-ba’i gtam brgya,), 36 ff.
Ngulchu Dharma Bhadra (dNgul-chu Dharma bhadra,), 1772-1851. A Brief Explanation and Outline of the Work entitled Fine Intentions (mDun legs-ma’i sa-bcad bsdus-don,), ACIP S06368-5, ff. 8a-9a.

Kyabje Pabongka Rinpoche Dechen Nyingpo (sKyabs-rje Pha-bong-kha rin-po-che bDe-chen snying-po,), 1878-1941. The Key that Opens the Door to the Excellent Path: Notes of an Explanation Granted when the Holder of the Diamond, the Good and Glorious Pabongka, Granted Profound Teachings upon the “Three Principal Paths” (rDo-rje-‘chang Pha-bong-kha-pa dpal bzang pos Lam-gtzo’i zab-khrid stzal skabs kyi gsung-bshad zin-bris Lam-bzang sgo-‘byed,), ACIP S00034, 41 ff.

His Holiness the First Panchen Lama, Lobsang Chukyi Gyeltsen (Pa -chen Blo-bzang chos kyi rgyal-mtsan,), 1565-1662. A Commentary to “The Three Realms,” Illuminating the Meaning of its Words (Sa-gsum-ma’i ’ikka tsig-don gsal-ba,), ACIP S05889, 15 ff.

His Holiness the Second Panchen Lama, Lobsang Yeshe (Pa-chen bla-ma sku-phreng gnyis-pa Blo-bzang ye-shes,), 1663-1737. The Essence of Eloquence: An Explanation of the “Three Principal Paths” which Captures the Crucial Points of All Scripture (Lam gyi gtzo-bo rnam gsum gyi rnam-bshad gsung-rab kun gyi gnad bsdus-pa Legs-bshad snying-po,), ACIP S12171, 60 ff.

His Holiness the Third Panchen Lama, Pelden Yeshe (Pa-chen bla-ma sku-phreng gsum-pa dPal-ldan ye-shes,), 1738-1780. Writings on the Subjects of the Catalogs to Newly Constructed Shrines; Descriptions accompanying Images; Colophons to Newly Printed Books, and the Like (rTen gsar-bzhengs kyi dkar-chag dang rgyab-yig zhal-byang sogs kyi skor,), ACIP S12234, 40 ff.

His Holiness the Fourth Panchen Lama, Tenpay Nyima (Pa-chen sku-phreng bzhi-pa bsTan-pa’i nyi-ma,), 1782-1853. The String of Lapis Beads: A Record of Instruction Received in Both the Profound and the Far-Reaching Sides of the Teaching (Zab-pa dang rgya-che-ba’i chos kyi thob-yig Bee∂’urya’i ‘phreng ba,), ACIP S12024, 241 ff.

Panchen Sunam Drakpa (Pa-chen bSod-nams grags-pa,), 1478-1554. Master Jamyang Shepa states that he utilized this author’s religious history for the text of the paintings; the Lovely Jewel for the Mind: A Spiritual History of the Earlier and Later Keepers of the Word, the Kadampas (bKa’-gdams gsar-rnying gi chos-‘byung Yid kyi mdzes-rgyan,), ACIP S12403, 162 ff.

Pelden Yeshe (dPal-ldan ye-shes,), n.d. Part Two of the “String of Moons”: A Biography which Illuminates the Holy Actions of Body, Speech, and Mind performed by that Great Keeper of the Diamond, His Holiness the Panchen Lama, the Omniscient One, Lobsang Yeshe, Good and Glorious (rDo-rje-’chang chen-po Pa -chen thams-cad mkhyen-pa Blo-bzang ye-shes dpal bzang-po’i sku gsung thugskyimdzad-pama-lus-pagsal-barbyed-pa’irnam-par thar-pa ‘Od-dkar can gyi ‘phreng-ba’i smad-cha,), ACIP SD12216, 137 ff.

Karnak Lotsawa Peljor Gyatso (mKhar-nag lo-tz’a-ba dPal-‘byor rgya-mtso,), b. 16th century. The Wish-Giving Tree: A Religious History of the Tradition of the Virtuous Ones (dGe-ldan chos-‘byung dPag-bsam ljon-pa,), 99 ff. Mentioned by Master Jamyang Shepa as one of his sources for the text of the paintings, and listed by Longdol Lama. Also referred to as the dGa’-ldan chos-‘byung.

Kuntun Peljor Hlundrup of Pabongka (Pha-bong-kha-pa ‘Khon-ston dPal-‘byor lhun-grub,), said in the Great Dictionary to have composed his chronicles in 1614. These are described in MHTL as The Annals of Pabongka, including a Listing of Religious Objects and an Historical Description (Pha-bong-kha-pa’i dkar-chag rnam-thar chos-‘byung deb-ther,). Master Jamyang Shepay Dorje mentions having used this author’s “religious history” as a source for the text of the paintings.

Tri Rinpoche Rinchen U-ser (Khri rin-po-che Rin-chen ‘od-zer,), 1453-1540. His Lamp that Illuminates the Chronicles of the Teachings (bsTan-rtzis gsal-ba’i sgron-me,) said by Master Jamyang Shepay Dorje to be one of his sources for the text of the paintings.

Sanggye Rinchen (Sangs-rgyas rin-chen,), n.d. The Story of How Je Tsongkapa met Hlodrak Drupchen, and How He Gave Some of His Precious Teeth to Kedrup Je (Lho-brag grub-chen dang mjal tsul, mKhas-grub rje la tsems gnang skor,) ACIP S05264, 4 ff.

Savitsky, Lev Serafimovich, with Vladimir Uspensky, Ngawang Khetsun, Jampa Namdol, Geshe Thupten Pelgye, Geshe Michael Roach, and John Brady (modern). A Catalog to the Tibetan Manuscript Collection of the Oriental Library of the St Petersburg Branch of the Russian Academy of Sciences, ACIP R01003.

W.D. Shakabpa (Zhva-sgab-pa dBang-phyug bde-ldan,), 1907-1989. Volume 1 of A Lake in which a Hundred Thousand Moons are Reflected, otherwise known as The Ocean of Pleasure in which Bees of Fresh Minds Play: A Clear Presentation of the Chronicles of Secular History for the Great Nation, as a Part of both the Religious and Secular History of the Land of Snows, Tibet (Gangs-ljongs bod-chos srid gnyis ldan gyi ^rgyal-khab chen-po’i srid-don gyi rgyal-rabs gsal-bar ston-pa Zla-ba ‘bum-phrag ‘char-ba’i rdzing-bu’am, Blo-gsar bung-ba dga’-ba’i rol-mtso zhes-bya-ba’i glegs-bam dang-po,), ACIP S12304, 685 pp.

Sumbha Kenpo Yeshe Peljor (Sumbha mkhan- po Ye-shes dpal-’byor,), 1704-1788. The Section which Describes How the Holy Dharma Spread in Tibet, the Land of Snows, from the “Excellent Wish-Giving Tree,” an Explanation by Sumbha Kenpo Yeshe Peljor of How the Jewel of the Holy Dharma Spread in India, the Land of the Realized; in the Great Land of China; in the Snowy Land of Tibet; and in Mongolia (Sumbha mkhan-po Ye-shes dpal-’byor gyi gsung, rGya-gar ‘phags-yul, rgya-nag chen- po, gangs-can bod-yul, sog-yul rnams su dam-chos rin-chen byung-tsul dPag-bsam ljon-bzang las, Gangs-can bod kyi yul du dam-chos dar-tsul gyi dpe-deb,), ACIP S12263, 377 pp.

Tokdenpa Jampel Gyatso (rTogs-ldan-pa ‘Jam-dpal rgya-mtso,), 1356-1428. The Compendium of Eloquent Explanantion: An Addendum to the Great Biography of the Venerable Tsongkapa (rJe-btzun Tzong-kha-pa’i rnam-thar chen-mo’i zur-‘debs Legs-bshad kun-‘dus,), ACIP S05260, 11 ff.

Kyabje Trijang Rinpoche Lobsang Yeshe Tendzin Gyatso (sKyabs-rje Khri-byang Rin-po-che Blo-bzang ye-shes bstan-’dzin rgya-mtso,), 1901-1981. An Anthology of Catalogs describing the Contents of a Variety of Sacred Images such as the Statue of Loving One, the Statue of Silk, and Others (Byams-sku dang gos-sku sogs kyi dkar-chag sna-tsogs phyogs gcig tu bkod-pa,), ACIP S00239, 44 ff.

Yongdzin Yeshe Gyeltsen (Yongs-‘dzin Ye-shes rgyal-mtsan,), 1713-1793. A Rosary of Excellent Jewels: Biographies of the Lamas of the Lineage of the Teachings on the Steps of the Path, the Ultimate Gem to Adorn the Word of the Victorious Buddhas (Byang-chub lam gyi rim-pa’i bla-ma brgyud-pa’i rnam-par thar-pa rGyal-bstan mdzes- pa’i rgyan-mchog phul-byung nor-bu’i phreng-ba,), ACIP S05985, 474 ff. The section on Je Tsongkapa is found in the Tibetan Cultural Printing Press editon on pp. 307-386.

Various authors (modern). A Brief Description of the Life of the First Incarnation of the Jamshe Line, Jamyang Shepay Dorje (‘Jam-bzhad sku-phreng dang-po ‘Jam-dbyangs bzhad-pa’i rdo-rje’i lo-rgyus nyung-bsdus,), p. 129 in The Treasure of Knowable Things, a Compendium of Catalogs to the Individual Collected Works of More than 180 Different Masters from All the Traditions of Tibetan Buddhism (Bod gangs-can gyi grub-mtha’ ris-med kyi mkhas-dbang brgya dang brgyad-cu lhag gi gsung-‘bum so-so’i dkar-chag phyogs gcig tu bsgrigs-pa Shes-bya’i gter-mdzod,), Vol. 2, ACIP R00010, 621 pp.

(No author mentioned). A Commentary upon the Biography and Supplication of the Victorious Buddha, Tsongkapa, entitled “The Immutable, Supreme and Ever-Reaching” (rGyal-ba Tzong-kha-pa’i rnam-thar gsol-‘debs Mi-‘gyur mchog yangs-ma’i ‘grel pa,), 28 ff. A biography listed by Longdol Lama (B64).
